title: Vivere all'estero
sub: Be used to, get used to, verb patterns e articoli - burocrazia e email formale
grammar: Be used to / get used to, verb patterns avanzati (-ing / to + infinito), articoli generici e zero article
situation: Burocrazia: affitto, residenza, sanità e banca all'estero

lessons.title: Abituarsi: used to, get used to e verb patterns
lessons.intro: Chi vive all'estero deve abituarsi a cose nuove: per dirlo servono be used to e get used to, che non vanno confusi con used to. In più: dopo quale verbo si usa -ing e dopo quale to + infinito, e quando l'articolo non ci vuole.

steps.title: Used to, be used to, get used to
steps.body:
Tre strutture che si assomigliano ma significano cose diverse:
- **used to + infinito**: abitudine o stato nel passato, ora finito. I **used to live** in Rome. (non vivo più lì)
- **be used to + -ing / nome**: essere abituato. I'**m used to getting up** early. (per me è normale)
- **get used to + -ing / nome**: abituarsi, il processo. I'm **getting used to driving** on the left.

In **be / get used to** la parola **to è una preposizione**: dopo ci vuole il gerundio o un nome, mai l'infinito. Anche **look forward to**, **object to**, **in addition to** funzionano così.
Negativa e domanda di used to: I **didn't use to** like coffee. / **Did** you **use to** play tennis?
Per le abitudini passate si può usare anche **would** (When I was young, we would swim every day), ma non per gli stati: «I would live in Rome» è sbagliato.
**Errori tipici degli italiani**: «I'm used to live alone», «I used to living here», «I am used to» al posto di «I got used to» per un cambiamento.
ex: I used to live in a small village.
Una volta vivevo in un piccolo villaggio.
She isn't used to the cold weather yet.
Non è ancora abituata al freddo.
It took him a month to get used to working nights.
Gli ci è voluto un mese per abituarsi a lavorare di notte.

steps.title: -ing o to + infinito?
steps.body:
Il verbo che precede decide la forma del verbo successivo.
- **+ -ing**: enjoy, avoid, suggest, admit, deny, risk, keep, mind, consider, can't help, it's no use, be worth, look forward to. She **avoided answering**. / I'm **looking forward to meeting** you.
- **+ to + infinito**: decide, refuse, promise, manage, afford, hope, plan, offer, agree, seem. He **refused to pay**.
- **+ oggetto + to + infinito**: persuade, allow, advise, remind, warn, invite, force, expect, want. They **allowed us to stay**.
- **make / let + oggetto + infinito senza to**: She **made me wait**. / They **let us go**. Al passivo make riprende to: I **was made to wait**.
- **suggest** non vuole mai to + infinito: She **suggested going** (o: suggested that we go).

**Errori tipici degli italiani**: «I suggest to go», «He decided leaving», «She allowed me going», «I look forward to see you».
ex: She suggested meeting at the station.
Ha suggerito di incontrarci in stazione.
The landlord refused to return the deposit.
Il padrone di casa ha rifiutato di restituire la caparra.
My boss made me work all weekend.
Il capo mi ha fatto lavorare tutto il fine settimana.

steps.title: Verbi con -ing e to + infinito: cambia il significato
steps.body:
Alcuni verbi accettano entrambe le forme, ma con **significato diverso**:
- **remember / forget + -ing**: ricordo / dimentico un fatto passato. I remember **locking** the door. (l'ho fatto, me lo ricordo)
- **remember / forget + to + inf.**: ricordo / dimentico di fare qualcosa. I forgot **to lock** the door. (non l'ho fatto)
- **stop + -ing**: smettere. He stopped **smoking**. / **stop + to + inf.**: fermarsi per fare. He stopped **to smoke**.
- **try + -ing**: provare come esperimento. Try **restarting** the computer. / **try + to + inf.**: sforzarsi. I tried **to open** it but couldn't.
- **regret + -ing**: rimpiangere. I regret **telling** her. / **regret + to + inf.**: spiacersi di dover (formale). We regret **to inform** you...
- **go on + -ing**: continuare. / **go on + to + inf.**: passare a fare dopo. She went on **to become** a doctor.

Con i verbi di percezione: **see him leave** (l'ho visto uscire, tutto) / **see him leaving** (l'ho visto mentre usciva).
ex: I remember meeting him at a conference.
Ricordo di averlo incontrato a una conferenza.
Remember to bring your passport.
Ricordati di portare il passaporto.
She stopped to look at the map.
Si è fermata a guardare la mappa.

steps.title: Articoli: generici, specifici e zero article
steps.body:
Per parlare **in generale** di plurali e nomi non numerabili l'inglese **non usa l'articolo**:
- **Life** abroad can be lonely. / **Prices** are high. / **Italians** love coffee. (non «The life», «The prices»)

Si usa **the** quando è chiaro quale: **The prices** in this city are high. / **The people** I met were friendly. Si usa the anche per cose uniche (the sun, the government), per i superlativi, per aggettivi che indicano gruppi (**the unemployed**) e per nazioni al plurale o con Republic/Kingdom (**the Netherlands, the UK**).

**Niente articolo** in alcune espressioni fisse: go **home**, go to **work**, **at** school / **in** hospital / **in** bed (come luoghi per la loro funzione), **by** bus / **by** car, **in** summer, **for** breakfast. Con un lavoro si usa **a / an**: She's **an** engineer.
**Errori tipici degli italiani**: «The life is expensive», «I go to the home», «She is engineer», «I have a flu» (si dice I have flu oppure I have the flu).
ex: Life abroad is not always easy.
La vita all'estero non è sempre facile.
The prices in this city are high.
I prezzi in questa città sono alti.
She works as an engineer in the Netherlands.
Lavora come ingegnere nei Paesi Bassi.

steps.why: Abitudine passata ormai finita: used to + infinito.

Life in abroad can be lonely.

lessons.title: Vivere all'estero
lessons.intro: Lessico per chi si trasferisce: shock culturale, affitto e burocrazia. Sono le parole che servono per leggere un contratto, riempire un modulo e raccontare la tua esperienza.

ex: She suffered from culture shock during her first month in Tokyo.
Ha sofferto di shock culturale durante il primo mese a Tokyo.
words.note: Non numerabile: culture shock, mai «a culture shock».

ex: He felt homesick during his first winter abroad.
Si sentiva nostalgico di casa durante il suo primo inverno all'estero.
It took the children a few weeks to settle in at their new school.
I bambini hanno impiegato qualche settimana ad ambientarsi nella nuova scuola.
Learning the language helped him integrate into the community.
Imparare la lingua lo ha aiutato a integrarsi nella comunità.
There is a large expat community in Lisbon.
A Lisbona c'è una grande comunità di espatriati.
My landlord has promised to repair the heating.
Il mio padrone di casa ha promesso di riparare il riscaldamento.
The tenants must pay the rent by the first of each month.
Gli inquilini devono pagare l'affitto entro il primo di ogni mese.
Read the tenancy agreement carefully before you sign it.
Leggi con attenzione il contratto d'affitto prima di firmarlo.
words.note: In UK anche rental agreement o lease.

ex: You will get your deposit back if the flat is left clean.
Riavrai la cauzione se l'appartamento viene lasciato pulito.
words.note: Attenzione: anche «deposito in banca», ma qui è la somma lasciata al padrone di casa.

ex: Citizens of some countries need a residence permit to work here.
I cittadini di alcuni paesi hanno bisogno di un permesso di soggiorno per lavorare qui.
The paperwork took longer than the move itself.
Le pratiche hanno richiesto più tempo del trasloco stesso.
Starting a business here involves a lot of red tape.
Avviare un'attività qui comporta molta burocrazia.
words.note: Ha sempre senso negativo; non numerabile.

ex: You'll soon get the hang of the ticket machines.
Presto ci prenderai la mano con le biglietterie automatiche.
The bank asked for proof of address, such as a utility bill.
La banca ha chiesto un documento che provi l'indirizzo, come una bolletta.

steps.s: Every month I pay the rent directly to my ___ .
steps.why: Chi riceve l'affitto è il landlord; chi lo paga è il tenant.

steps.s: It took me six months to get the ___ of the bus system.
steps.why: L'espressione è get the hang of.

steps.s: Immigrants who learn the language often find it easier to ___ into society.
steps.why: Integrate into = integrarsi in.

steps.s: The ___ of foreign workers into the team was surprisingly smooth.
steps.why: Serve un nome: integrate -> integration.

opts: Triste perché si ha nostalgia di casa
steps.why: Homesick = nostalgia di casa e famiglia.

lessons.title: Quello che nessuno ti dice
lessons.intro: Il post di un blog scritto da una donna italiana trasferita a Dublino: shock culturale, burocrazia e solitudine. Nel testo trovi be used to, get used to e molte espressioni utili per raccontare un'esperienza.

steps.title: What nobody tells you about moving abroad
steps.text:
When I accepted a job in Dublin two years ago, I was convinced that the move would be easy. I spoke English reasonably well, the flight from Turin took less than three hours, and my new employer had even arranged a flat. What I had not expected was the culture shock, which arrived not in the first week, when everything felt like a holiday, but in the third month.

The first surprise was the weather, or rather my relationship with it. I was used to hot, dry summers and clear winters, so grey drizzle that could last for days left me exhausted. Then there was the food. Eating dinner at six o'clock seemed to me completely absurd, yet that was when my colleagues went home and, worse, when the canteen closed. Within a few weeks I had stopped fighting it, although I still cannot get used to having a sandwich as a proper lunch.

Paperwork was a different story. At home I had always complained about bureaucracy, but I discovered that every country has its own version. To open a bank account I needed proof of address, and to get proof of address I needed a bank account. It took three visits, two phone calls and a very patient neighbour, who lent me an old utility bill, before the problem was solved. Eventually I got the hang of the system, and I now carry a folder with copies of everything, just in case.

The hardest part, however, was loneliness. People were friendly, but friendliness is not the same as friendship. Colleagues would say, "We should grab a coffee sometime," and I would wait for an invitation that never came. It took me months to realise that this was simply a polite way of saying hello. Once I understood, I began suggesting specific plans, and things changed. I joined a climbing club, volunteered at a language café and, little by little, built a circle of friends.

If I could give advice to anyone thinking of moving abroad, it would be this. Do not expect to feel at home immediately: it can take a year or more to settle in. Learn the local customs before you start judging them. Keep in touch with people at home, but avoid comparing everything with the way things are done there, because it will only make you miserable. And be patient with yourself. Nobody adapts perfectly, and a little homesickness is a sign that you cared about the life you left.

Today, I would not go back. Dublin has become a place where I am no longer a guest but a resident, someone who complains about the rain with the same enthusiasm as everybody else. I still miss my family, my mother's cooking and the sound of my own language in the street. But I have learnt that being at home is not about a place; it is about the people you find, and the effort you make to meet them halfway.

qs.q: When did the writer's culture shock begin?
qs.why: «not in the first week... but in the third month».

qs.q: Which food-related habit does she still find difficult?
opts: Having a sandwich as a proper lunch
qs.why: «I still cannot get used to having a sandwich as a proper lunch».

qs.q: Why was it difficult to open a bank account?
opts: She needed proof of address, which she could only get with an account.
qs.why: «to get proof of address I needed a bank account».

qs.q: How does she deal with paperwork now?
opts: She keeps a folder with copies of everything.
She asks her neighbour to do it.
qs.why: «I now carry a folder with copies of everything».

qs.q: What did she misunderstand about her colleagues?
opts: She thought a casual coffee suggestion was a real invitation.
She believed they worked too much.
She did not understand their accent.
qs.why: «I would wait for an invitation that never came»: era un modo gentile di salutare.

qs.q: What did she do to make friends?
opts: She joined a climbing club and volunteered at a language café.
She invited her family to visit.
qs.why: «I joined a climbing club, volunteered at a language café».

qs.q: Which advice does the writer give?
opts: Compare the new country with your own.
Learn the local customs before judging them.
Avoid contact with people at home.
Expect to settle in within a month.
qs.why: «Learn the local customs before you start judging them».

qs.q: Being at home depends on the ___ you find and the effort you make.
qs.why: «it is about the people you find».

steps.q: Nel testo, «get the hang of» significa:
steps.why: Get the hang of something = imparare a farlo bene.

steps.s: She still cannot get used to ___ a sandwich for lunch.
steps.why: Get used to + -ing.

steps.s: It can take a year or more to settle ___ .
steps.why: Settle in = ambientarsi.

steps.q: «Colleagues would say, "We should grab a coffee sometime"» usa would per indicare:
steps.why: Would (non used to) per ripetute azioni abituali nel passato.

lessons.title: All'ufficio anagrafe
lessons.intro: Un italiano trasferito in Inghilterra va in comune a registrarsi come residente. Ascolta quali documenti servono, quanto costa il certificato e perché gli serve.

steps.title: Registering at the town hall
steps.it: Ascolta la conversazione. Puoi riascoltarla e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Good morning. Can I help you?
Good morning. I've just moved to Leeds from Italy and I'd like to register as a resident. Do I need an appointment?
Normally yes, but we're quiet this morning, so I can see you now. Have you brought your documents?
I think so. I've got my passport and my tenancy agreement. I wasn't sure what else to bring.
That's a good start. We also need proof of your address, such as a utility bill, but a tenancy agreement signed by your landlord is fine. Is your name on it?
Yes, it is. I rent a room in a shared house, and the landlord signed it last week.
Perfect. And are you working or studying?
Working. I'm a physiotherapist at the city hospital. I started on the first of the month.
Then you'll also need to register with a doctor. That's a separate process, but you can do it at any local surgery. Just take your passport and this form.
Is there a fee for the registration?
No, it's free. But if you want a certificate to prove that you live here, it's fifteen pounds. Most banks ask for one.
Actually, that's why I'm here. I'm trying to open a bank account and they want proof of residence.
In that case, I'd get the certificate. It will be posted to you within five working days, so make sure someone is at home to collect it. Now, could you fill in this form in capital letters, please?
Of course. Where do I write the date I arrived?
Here, at the top. And sign at the bottom.
Done. Thank you very much for your help.
You're welcome. Good luck with the new job.

qs.why: «I've just moved to Leeds from Italy».

qs.q: Why can Mrs Evans see him without an appointment?
opts: He is a friend of the family.
The office is quiet that morning.
qs.why: «we're quiet this morning, so I can see you now».

qs.q: Which document does Mrs Evans accept as proof of address?
opts: A tenancy agreement signed by the landlord
qs.why: «a tenancy agreement signed by your landlord is fine».
«I'm a physiotherapist at the city hospital».

qs.q: Why does Marco need the certificate?
qs.why: «I'm trying to open a bank account and they want proof of residence».

qs.q: How long will the certificate take to arrive?
qs.why: «posted to you within five working days».

steps.en: I've just moved here from Italy and I'd like to register as a resident.
steps.it: Mi sono appena trasferito qui dall'Italia e vorrei registrarmi come residente.

steps.en: Could you fill in this form in capital letters, please?
steps.it: Potrebbe compilare questo modulo in stampatello, per favore?

steps.en: Do I need to make an appointment?

lessons.title: Burocrazia all'estero
lessons.intro: Affitto, residenza, medico e banca: le richieste che servono per sbrigare le pratiche in un paese straniero, con il tono giusto e le domande che evitano brutte sorprese.

steps.title: Affittare e registrarsi
steps.body:
Frasi utili per un appartamento e per le pratiche:
- **I'm interested in the flat advertised online.** = Sono interessato all'appartamento in annuncio.
- **Is the rent inclusive of bills?** = L'affitto comprende le utenze?
- **How much is the deposit, and when will it be returned?** = Quanto è la cauzione e quando verrà restituita?
- **Is there a minimum tenancy?** = C'è una durata minima del contratto?
- **Could you send me the tenancy agreement before I sign?** = Può mandarmi il contratto prima della firma?
- **Who is responsible for repairs?** = Chi si occupa delle riparazioni?
- **I'd like to register as a resident.** = Vorrei registrarmi come residente.

Per chiedere chiarimenti: **Sorry, could you explain what that means?** / **Would you mind writing that down?**
ex: Is the rent inclusive of bills?
L'affitto comprende le utenze?
Who is responsible for repairs?
Chi è responsabile delle riparazioni?

steps.title: In banca e dal medico
steps.body:
Alla banca:
- **I'd like to open a current account.** = Vorrei aprire un conto corrente.
- **What documents do I need to bring?**
- **Is there a monthly fee?** / **Is there an overdraft facility?**
- **How long will it take for the card to arrive?**

Dal medico (UK: **GP** = medico di base, **surgery** = ambulatorio):
- **I'd like to register with a GP.**
- **I'd like to make an appointment, please.**
- **I've been having headaches for a week.** = Ho mal di testa da una settimana.
- **Could I have a prescription for these?** = Può prescrivermi questi farmaci?

**Errore tipico degli italiani**: «I have an appointment to the doctor» (dal medico: **with** the doctor / at the surgery).
ex: I'd like to open a current account.
Vorrei aprire un conto corrente.
I'd like to register with a GP.
Vorrei iscrivermi presso un medico di base.

steps.title: Viewing a flat
steps.it: Scegli la battuta più naturale e cortese.
lines: So, this is the room. The rent is five hundred pounds a month.

opts: It's lovely. Is the rent inclusive of bills?
Five hundred? Too expensive, I pay four hundred.
Is nice. The bills are included or no?

lines: Water and heating are included, but not electricity or internet.

opts: I see. And how much is the deposit, and when will it be returned?
I want that you give me the deposit back immediately.
What is the deposit? You keep it?

lines: It's one month's rent, and you get it back within ten days after you leave.

opts: That sounds fair. Could you send me the tenancy agreement before I sign?
Fine, give me the keys now.
I need to sign nothing, I trust you.

steps.why: Domande dirette ma cortesi (Is the rent inclusive of bills? / Could you send me...) mostrano che conosci le cose da chiedere prima di firmare.

lines: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

opts: Good afternoon. I'd like to open a current account, please.
I want a bank account, fast.
Hello, I have the necessity to a conto.

lines: Certainly. Do you have proof of address and some form of ID?

opts: I've brought my passport and my tenancy agreement. Is that enough?
I have the passport. The rest I don't have.

lines: That's fine. The account has no monthly fee, and your card will arrive within a week.

opts: Perfect. What happens if I need to withdraw more than my balance?
No fee? Then there is a trick, surely.
Okay, I'm waiting here for the card.

pairs: Is the rent inclusive of bills?
Could you send me the tenancy agreement?
I'd like to open a current account.
What documents do I need to bring?
I'd like to register with a doctor.

steps.it: Quando mi verrà restituita la caparra?
steps.en: When will the deposit be returned to me
Is the rent inclusive of bills?

steps.q: You are renting a flat abroad. Phone the landlord to ask about the rent, the deposit and the contract, and to arrange a viewing.
steps.it: Telefona al padrone di casa: chiedi dell'affitto, della cauzione, del contratto e concorda una visita (almeno 5 frasi).
hints: Is the rent inclusive of bills?
Would it be possible to see the flat on...?
steps.model: Hello, I'm calling about the flat advertised online. Is it still available? I'd like to know whether the rent is inclusive of bills, and how much the deposit is. Could you also tell me how long the minimum tenancy is? If possible, I'd like to see the flat on Saturday morning. And could you send me the tenancy agreement beforehand, so that I can read it carefully?

lessons.title: L'email formale a un ufficio
lessons.intro: Scriverai un'email formale a un ufficio pubblico per chiedere informazioni e un appuntamento. Struttura, formule e registro sono quelli richiesti anche nella prova di scrittura del B2 First.

steps.title: L'email formale a un ufficio
steps.body:
Una buona email formale è breve, chiara e cortese. La struttura:
- **Oggetto** chiaro: Enquiry about resident registration.
- **Saluto**: Dear Sir or Madam, (o Dear Mr / Ms + cognome se lo conosci).
- **Scopo** nella prima frase: I am writing to enquire about... / to request... / to confirm...
- **Dettagli**: chi sei e qual è la tua situazione, in modo sintetico.
- **Richieste** cortesi: Could you please let me know...? / I would be grateful if you could...
- **Chiusura**: Thank you in advance for your help. / I look forward to hearing from you.
- **Formula finale**: Yours faithfully (senza nome del destinatario) o Yours sincerely (con nome). Nelle email si accetta anche Kind regards.

**Evita**: contrazioni (I'm, can't), espressioni colloquiali, punti esclamativi, frasi come «I want to know». Con un verbo dopo **look forward to** serve -ing: I look forward to **hearing** from you.
ex: I am writing to enquire about the procedure for registration.
Scrivo per informarmi sulla procedura di registrazione.
I would be grateful if you could confirm the fee.
Le sarei grato se potesse confermarmi la tariffa.

steps.q: Quale frase è adatta a un'email formale a un ufficio?
opts: I would be grateful if you could confirm the opening hours.
Can you tell me the opening hours?
Tell me when you are open.
steps.why: Il condizionale con grateful if you could è la formula più cortese.

steps.s: Please let me ___ whether I need to book an appointment.
steps.why: Let me know = fammi sapere.

steps.s: I am looking forward to hear from you.
answers: I am looking forward to hearing from you
I look forward to hearing from you
steps.why: Look forward to è seguito da -ing: to è una preposizione.

steps.q: You have recently moved to another country and need to register as a resident. Write an email to the local registration office. Say who you are, ask which documents you need, whether there is a fee, and request an appointment at a convenient time.
steps.it: Scrivi un'email formale all'ufficio anagrafe (140-190 parole): presentati brevemente, chiedi quali documenti servono, se c'è una tariffa, e proponi gli orari per un appuntamento. Non usare contrazioni.
checklist: Contenuto: ho spiegato la situazione, chiesto i documenti, la tariffa e l'appuntamento
Comunicazione: registro formale costante, nessuna contrazione, saluto e chiusura adatti
Organizzazione: oggetto, scopo, dettagli, richieste, chiusura in paragrafi distinti
Lingua: ho usato almeno una formula con I would be grateful if you could e look forward to + -ing
Ho rispettato il numero di parole (140-190)
useful: I am writing to enquire about...
Could you please let me know...?
I would be grateful if you could...
Thank you in advance for your help.
I look forward to hearing from you.
steps.model:
Subject: Enquiry about resident registration

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to enquire about the procedure for registering as a resident in your city. I moved here from Italy on 1 September to start a job at the university, and I am renting a flat in Highfield Road.

Could you please let me know which documents I need to bring with me? I have my passport, a signed tenancy agreement and a letter from my employer, but I am not sure whether these are sufficient. I would also be grateful if you could tell me whether there is a fee, and whether I can make an appointment online or must visit the office in person.

Since I work during the day, I would prefer an appointment early in the morning or after five o'clock. If this is not possible, please let me know about any other options.

Thank you in advance for your help. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Marco Bianchi

steps.q: Tell me about a time when you had to deal with bureaucracy. What was difficult?
steps.it: Racconta una volta in cui hai dovuto affrontare la burocrazia: che cos'era difficile e com'è finita (almeno 5 frasi).
hints: What I found most difficult was...
steps.model: Last year I had to renew my residence permit. I had to queue for two hours, only to be told that I had forgotten one document. What I found most difficult was that nobody could explain exactly which form I needed. In the end, I went back the next day with a folder full of copies, and everything was sorted out in ten minutes.

steps.q: Imagine you are going to live in another country. What do you think you would find hardest to get used to?
steps.it: Immagina di trasferirti all'estero: a che cosa faresti più fatica ad abituarti e perché (almeno 5 frasi).
hints: I think I would find it hard to get used to...
I'd soon get the hang of...
steps.model: I think I would find it hardest to get used to the food and the lunchtimes. I'm used to having a long lunch with my family, so a quick sandwich would feel strange. On the other hand, I'd soon get the hang of the language, because I like speaking with people. I would probably feel homesick for the first few months, but I am sure I would settle in.
